summary: A humorous account of organizing the Neighborhood Fun Run scheduled for September 10, 2023, which began as an idea from Bobbie Jenkins in the neighborhood group chat. The piece recounts the planning chaos, including permits, sponsorships, a makeshift timing system, costumes, overeager volunteers, rogue bands and cheerleaders, and refreshment stations that turned into food festivals.
one_line: A comedic behind-the-scenes look at planning the quirky Neighborhood Fun Run on September 10, 2023, from permits and sponsors to costumes and food stations.
key_facts: The Neighborhood Fun Run is slated for a morning on September 10, 2023.
Bobbie Jenkins started the idea in the neighborhood group chat after returning from a motivational walking seminar, typing "Why don't we host our own fun run?"
Organizers faced permit applications and safety regulations; cordoning off Mrs. Harrison's prized rose bush would require a city council meeting.
Water station duties clashed with the weekly watering schedule of local flora aficionado Tom Green.
Jerry McFinnigan, described as able to sell ice to an Eskimo, helped win sponsors from local businesses.
The local taxidermist agreed to donate coupons for 10% off your next stuffed badger as runner prizes.
The race timer was old Casio watches duct-taped together; Carol from IT set up a makeshift system using bells, smartphone stopwatches and popsicle sticks to mark laps.
Sixty-year-old Herbert dressed as a banana while chasing his runaway Chihuahua, also dressed as a banana, through the route.
The Johnson twins showed up in full astronaut gear.
Larry, a retired drill sergeant living on Maple Drive, took traffic directing too seriously, using a whistle and airplane-gate arm gestures.
Local bands along the course turned the event into an impromptu battle of the bands, while the high school cheerleading squad chanted "Go Run, Go Stride, Go Conquer, Don't Hide!".
A local cat enthusiast let her cats join in, creating a 'catwalk' section, and rookie baker Janet's energy bars turned out to be nap-inducing, as tested on her husband.
Pete's Pizzeria offered mid-run slices and Sarah's Smoothies showcased a kale and spirulina super blend at the refreshment stations.
